# Boundary health endpoints

Boundary provides health monitoring through the `/health` path of a listener with the `ops` purpose. By default, a listener with that purpose runs on port `9203`.

Controllers and workers both serve a health endpoint, but they behave differently:

- The controller endpoint reports its status using the HTTP status code and returns an empty response body.
- The worker endpoint always returns `200 OK` and reports its status in the response body.

## Requirements

Both endpoints require a listener with the `ops` purpose in the configuration file of the server you want to monitor.

### Controller health requirements

To enable the controller health endpoint, the Boundary instance must be started with a controller. The configuration file must define a `controller` block, a listener with the `api` purpose, and a listener with the `ops` purpose. Under these conditions, Boundary exposes the `ops` server, which hosts the controller health API.

### Worker health requirements

To enable the worker health endpoint, define a listener with the `ops` purpose in the worker's own configuration file. The worker serves its own health endpoint; you do not query the controller to determine the health of a worker.

If a single Boundary instance runs both a controller and a worker, the instance serves the controller health endpoint. In that case, you can request worker information from the controller endpoint using the `worker_info` query parameter.

## Shutdown grace period

When the controller health endpoint is enabled, you can configure the controller to respond with `503 Service Unavailable` when it receives a shutdown signal. The controller then waits a configurable amount of time before starting the shutdown process.

This feature supports load-balanced deployments by reducing the risk that a shutting-down instance receives new requests. While the controller waits, it processes requests normally, but the health endpoint reports it as unhealthy. The load balancer can remove the unhealthy instance from the pool before shutdown proceeds.

The shutdown grace period is disabled by default. To enable it, set `graceful_shutdown_wait_duration` in the `controller` block of the configuration file. The value must be a duration string that [ParseDuration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) can parse, such as `"10s"`.

## Health API

The health service exposes a single read-only endpoint: `GET /health`. Controllers and workers respond differently.

The controller returns:

- `200 OK` when the api gRPC server is up
- `5xx` or a request timeout when it is unhealthy
- `503 Service Unavailable` when it is shutting down and waiting for the grace period

All controller responses have an empty body. `GET /health` does not accept any input on the controller.

The worker always returns `200 OK`. It returns an empty JSON object, `{}`, unless you include the `worker_info=1` query parameter. In that case the response body contains a `worker_process_info` object.

<Note>

The worker health endpoint always returns `200 OK`, even when the worker cannot reach its upstream. A health check that tests only the HTTP status code reports a disconnected worker as healthy.

To determine whether a worker is ready to proxy sessions, request the worker information and check the `upstream_connection_state` field. Refer to [Check the health endpoint](/boundary/docs/monitor/check-health-endpoint) for an example.

</Note>

For the full list of status codes, query parameters, and response fields, refer to the [health endpoint reference](/boundary/docs/monitor/health-reference).

## Example response

The following shows the response from a worker that is connected to its upstream:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```json
{
  "worker_process_info": {
    "state": "active",
    "active_session_count": 0,
    "upstream_connection_state": "READY"
  }
}
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

## Example configuration

The following examples show the listener stanzas that enable the health endpoint.

An example controller configuration:

```hcl
controller {
  name = "boundary-controller"
  database {
    url = "postgresql://<username>:<password>@10.0.0.1:5432/<database_name>"
  }
}

listener "tcp" {
  purpose     = "api"
  tls_disable = true
}

listener "tcp" {
  purpose     = "ops"
  tls_disable = true
}
```

An example worker configuration:

```hcl
worker {
  auth_storage_path = "/var/lib/boundary"
  initial_upstreams = ["10.0.0.1:9201"]
}

listener "tcp" {
  address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
  purpose = "proxy"
}

listener "tcp" {
  address     = "0.0.0.0:9203"
  purpose     = "ops"
  tls_disable = true
}
```

To enable a shutdown grace period, add `graceful_shutdown_wait_duration` to the `controller` block:

```hcl
controller {
  name = "boundary-controller"
  database {
    url = "env://BOUNDARY_PG_URL"
  }
  graceful_shutdown_wait_duration = "10s"
}
```

For a complete controller configuration, refer to [Controller configuration](/boundary/docs/configuration/controller#complete-configuration-example).
